Thought: To determine the point group of the molecule, I need to first understand its structure from the SMILES representation. The SMILES "C(=C(F)F)=C(F)F" corresponds to 1,1,2,2-tetrafluoroethene, which is a planar molecule with symmetry.

The SMILES structure implies a molecule with a central carbon-carbon double bond, each carbon bearing two fluorine atoms. The symmetry of this molecule must be determined by assessing the presence of symmetry elements such as planes of symmetry, axes of rotation, and centers of inversion.

1,1,2,2-tetrafluoroethene has a C2 axis along the line perpendicular to the plane of the molecule (through the center of the double bond), and two perpendicular mirror planes (σv) through each carbon and its attached fluorines.

This set of symmetry elements corresponds to the D2d point group.
